assumptions: This is a synthetic deterministic cyclic-schedule feasibility fixture, not an operator schedule or observed HAPS service campaign.

Five identical HAPS each follow a perfectly periodic 44-day lifecycle: 30 days on station and 14 sequential days in recovery, transport, inspection/refurbishment, ground-ready replenishment/preparation, launch and repositioning.
Start phases are 0, 8.8, 17.6, 26.4 and 35.2 days; the 5-platform rotation is perfectly staggered to target at least three simultaneous service units.
A 220-day evaluation window equals five 44-day cycles; the schedule is a finite repeated idealization.
There are three required service units; each on-station platform contributes one unit and off-station states contribute zero.
Only one maintenance bay, one launch slot, one recovery slot and one reposition slot are available; the 7-day planned maintenance segment is separated by at least 8.8 days between platforms.
The primary-only comparator uses HAPS-A/B/C under the same cyclic state timelines; the spare-rotation comparator uses all five platforms.
All power rates are synthetic. The reserve energy report includes only HAPS-D/E state power, not primary platform energy, payload, thermal, propulsion or network loads.
No common-cause weather event, independent failure, random repair duration, parts inventory constraint, service handover, backhaul failure or safety authorization is modeled.
This schedule is designed to test a feasible idealized staggered lower-bound case. It does not prove that such a rotation can be maintained in operational weather or real depot logistics.
